title: Union Find: Connectivity After Unions
contract: Return the number of components after all undirected union operations on n vertices.
brute: int[] label=new int[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)label[i]=i;int count=n;for(int[] edge:edges){int old=label[edge[1]],next=label[edge[0]];if(old!=next){for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(label[i]==old)label[i]=next;count--;}emit("Relabel an entire component","labels",label,"components",count);}return count;
optimal: int[] parent=new int[n],size=new int[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++){parent[i]=i;size[i]=1;}int count=n;for(int[] edge:edges){int a=find(parent,edge[0]),b=find(parent,edge[1]);if(a!=b){if(size[a]<size[b]){int t=a;a=b;b=t;}parent[b]=a;size[a]+=size[b];count--;}emit("Attach the smaller root and compress search paths","parents",parent,"sizes",size,"components",count);}return count;
reasoning: Quick-find labels make queries easy but a union may rewrite every vertex label.
Parent trees identify representatives; attach the smaller component to the larger to prevent tall trees.
Path compression during find flattens visited chains. Decrement components only when roots differ, so duplicate edges do not change the count.
